Why we're building this

Smart homes made us busier.

We were promised a home that looks after itself. We got a dozen apps, a drawer of chargers and a light that won't come on when the Wi-Fi drops.

The three of us have spent the last few years around AI. We think it can do something better than add another screen. It can notice what's happening in a room and simply deal with it, without asking you anything.

That's what v/h is for. We're starting with a lamp.

The shift

For 140 years, a smarter light meant more control.

Until now

A switch. A dimmer.
An app. A voice.

Every step gave you more to control. The lamp still had no idea you were in the room.

With v/h

A lamp that
understands.

It notices when you sit down and when you leave. It learns your routine, today's and tomorrow's. It looks after itself.

Why not an app?

Your phone was never a good light switch.

We've all done it. It's late, you want the lights down, so you pick up your phone. Here's what tends to happen next.

  • You open the app. Then the messages.

    One tap to dim the lights turns into scrolling long after the lights are down. The lamp was meant to help you wind down. The phone did the opposite.

  • The Wi-Fi drops. So does the light.

    When a lamp needs the internet to think, a bad connection means a lamp that won't do its one job.

  • The company moves on. The lamp stops working.

    Smart home devices have stopped working when the company behind them switched off its servers. You paid for it, it's still on your table, and it does nothing.

  • Your evenings end up on someone else's computer.

    Every time you come home, sit down or go to bed, a cloud-connected light can report it. That's a detailed picture of your life, kept somewhere you'll never see.

So we left all of it out. No app. No account. No internet needed. The lamp does its own thinking, and your routine never leaves your home.

How it works

Nothing to set up. Nothing to say.

  1. 1

    It notices.

    A sensor sees when you sit down nearby, and when you get up and go.

  2. 2

    It learns.

    An AI agent inside the lamp learns your patterns, the ones you have now and the ones coming next. Nothing goes to the cloud.

  3. 3

    It acts.

    It switches on when you need it and off when you don't. You never touch a setting.

  • You sit down with a book. The light is already on.
  • You get up and go to bed. It turns off behind you.
  • It's winter and dark by five. It's on before you reach your chair.
